author: kkrott87
quote:
Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is not just a remaster. It is a near-perfect realization of one of the greatest games ever made. From the moment you step out of Link’s house in Kokiri Forest, everything feels alive, precise, and magical. 
The controls are tight, the pacing is masterful, and every dungeon still delivers that perfect mix of exploration, puzzle-solving, and combat that defined a generation. The story remains timeless, simple on the surface, yet emotionally rich and unforgettable. What elevates this version is how beautifully it has been brought forward. 
The visuals look sharp and vibrant without losing the classic charm, the performance is flawless, and quality-of-life improvements make it even more enjoyable without changing what made the original special. It feels both nostalgic and fresh at the same time. Whether you’re playing it for the first time or returning after years, Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 stands as a remarkable achievement. It is a game that still defines what great adventure design looks like.
10/10. Perfect. A true masterpiece that every Switch 2 owner should experience.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: kkrott87
quote:
I was really looking forward to GTA VI, but after spending time with it, I have to say it falls short of what the series has delivered before. 
The story and lore feel underdeveloped compared to previous entries. 
Jason and Lucia come across as flat and lack the charisma that made characters like Michael, Franklin, Trevor, or even Niko memorable. It’s hard to get invested in them or their journey.Feature-wise, it feels stripped back. 
There are more limitations on what you can do, and the open-world freedom that defined earlier games is noticeably reduced. It doesn’t feel as unrestricted or playful as the previous titles. 
The tone also leans heavily into modern messaging that often pulls you out of the experience rather than enhancing it. Combined with the more restricted gameplay, it ends up feeling less like a GTA game and more like a more linear, guided experience. I still respect Rockstar’s craft, but this one didn’t live up to the standard set by the earlier games in the franchise.
